title: Jesse Minter Impressed With Jacoby Brissett's Quick Learning
headline: Jacoby Brissett looks set to play Monday night for Baltimore, with Minter praising how quickly he learned the offense. Lamar Jackson has had surgery and Minter gave no timeline.
summary: Minter opened by saying the team had a good week of preparation and is focused on Monday night. His only injury update was that safety Jaylinn Hawkins will miss the game, though he worked back in a bit this week and the team hopes to have him next week. Most of the session was about Jacoby Brissett, who just arrived. Minter said he was very impressed by how fast Brissett picked up the offense, with a clean practice operation and only a few timing issues to revisit. He added that this guarantees nothing, but he is excited to see him operate Monday. On Lamar Jackson, Minter confirmed the surgery happened and said the statement was meant to stop speculation. He declined to give a timeline beyond 'the timeline is the timeline', and said he and Lamar are on the same page. He also said the team feels refreshed after the long break, is focused on its identity, and has tried small pre-practice warm-up tweaks. Kicker Riley Patterson was praised after a chaotic week at the position. Adam Randall could be activated this week or next, and Minter called him a versatile player who could add a spark on kick return.

injuries.detail: Out for Monday night's game. He was able to work back in a little this week, and the team hopes to have him rolling next week.
He has had surgery. Minter gave no timeline and said only that the timeline is the timeline.
He could be activated this week or next, as the window runs through next week. Minter said it depends on what is best for the 53-man roster.

signals.claim: Will operate the offense (likely start at QB) in Monday night's game.
signals.note: Brissett looks to be the QB option Monday with Lamar Jackson recovering from surgery, and Minter says he has picked up the offense quickly.
signals.quote: very, very impressed with how fast he's learned what we're doing

signals.note: Jackson has had surgery and Minter gave no return timeline, so he is not a Monday option and his availability is uncertain.

signals.claim: Will miss Monday night's game and could return the following week.
signals.note: Hawkins is out, which matters for IDP and defensive depth.
signals.quote: Hawkins will be out this game.

topics.detail: Riley Patterson will kick Monday after a hectic week at the position. Minter praised his experience and past big kicks and expects him to kick well.

Asked about kick return, Minter called the player a versatile guy who has flashed in different roles and could add a spark. It is not explicit that he meant Randall, whom the question was about. Randall's activation window runs through next week.
Minter said the team is refreshed after the extended break, is focused on its identity in all three phases, and wants to carry the week's preparation into Monday night.
The team added a new pre-practice warm-up. Minter called it a small marginal gain meant to have players warmed up and ready, not a major change.

title: Jim Harbaugh on Tre Harris and the Team's Preparation for Monday Night Football
headline: Tre Harris is expected to be a bigger part of the receiver group, while an unnamed player is questionable for Monday night against Baltimore.
summary: Harbaugh met the media ahead of the Week 10 Monday Night Football game against the Ravens. He said one player, whom the captions don't identify, has been progressing but is questionable for the game after doing little in practice. On the receivers, he called Tre Harris very capable and said he is excited and ready to roll in what is expected to be a larger role. He said players who have been out for a while, with David Njoku named, are eager to return and bring good energy and 'fresh legs'. A reporter asked about a player named Denzel who hasn't played all season; the caption name doesn't match anyone on the roster. Harbaugh said Brenen Thompson, who has had a setback, is doing everything he can. For the game itself, he kept to his usual line that if the team plays well it will win. He stressed doing your job at a high level, not dwelling on past losses, and gave no scheme or depth chart specifics.

injuries.detail: Harbaugh said the player has made progress but is questionable for the game after doing little in practice this week.
Reporter referred to a setback he is working through; Harbaugh only said he is doing everything he can. No game status given.
Harbaugh named Njoku among players back after time out who are excited and bringing energy. No snap or role details given.
Reporter mentioned a 'Denzel' who hasn't played all season and is now back. No roster match, so the player can't be identified.

signals.claim: Will take on a larger role in the receiver group and be on the field against the Ravens.
signals.note: Harbaugh's confidence suggests more targets and snaps for Harris as the receiver group is reshuffled.

title: Exclusive: Kellen Moore previews Week 10 vs. Panthers
headline: Audric Estime impressed in the win over Cleveland and is expected to stay in the backfield mix. Cesar Ruiz slides to center, which implies Erik McCoy is out, and Tyler Shough's scrambling is a rushing-upside note.
summary: Coach Moore said the Saints' emphasis on the run game paid off against Cleveland, because controlling the line of scrimmage on offense and against the run affects every phase. He praised Audric Estime for arriving Tuesday night or Wednesday morning, retaining the game plan, and playing well. He said the team will need the whole running back group to support Tyler Shough. Moore said Shough's 51 rushing yards came from scrambling when chances appear, and added that Shough has to be smart about it. For Carolina, Cesar Ruiz will fill in at center. Moore called him a good, versatile player who has played guard and center in the NFL and in college. On Bryce Young, Moore spoke only in generalities: pressure in the pocket, the rush plan, and tight coverage. Moore downplayed the chance to take the division lead, saying the team takes it one week at a time while knowing division games matter.

injuries.detail: Moore did not name McCoy. Ruiz filling in at center, plus McCoy's DNP with a biceps injury on the report, implies McCoy is out.

signals.claim: Estime will keep a role in the Saints' running back rotation, as part of a backfield group Moore says is needed.
signals.note: He played well after joining midweek, so he is a rising waiver and depth option, although the backfield is crowded.
signals.quote: Really impressive for OD to show up

signals.claim: Shough will keep scrambling for yards when opportunities arise.
signals.note: His rushing production, 51 yards last week, adds quarterback fantasy upside, though Moore says he needs to be smart about it.
signals.quote: he's done a great job with it

signals.claim: Ruiz will start at center against Carolina.
signals.note: A steady interior line matters for the run game and Shough's protection, and Ruiz moving to center confirms McCoy's absence.
signals.quote: we feel fortunate to have a guy like him that can slide over there

topics.detail: Moore said the run game and run defense changed the Cleveland game by influencing the line of scrimmage. He called it a weekly battle.
Moore called Young a talented quarterback and gave no specifics beyond pressuring him in the pocket and keeping coverage tight.
A win would put the Saints atop the division. Moore said the team is aware of the standings but is focused on one week at a time.
